historical_reviews.deepseek: It recognizes the mutation and need for operator input, but a generic CLI parameter cannot establish raw payload equivalence or safe recovery after the OOB route moves.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly adds the OOB access-loss gate and retains this as a prerequisite-driven case rather than labeling it permanently blocked.
historical_reviews.history: The invalidated prior-run location was found but excluded as authority; the separately committed IB setter was examined to isolate the remote-channel risk unique to this record.
historical_reviews.v3_1: Reconnection must be tied to immutable target identity, not merely the first address that responds after DHCP/discovery changes.

original_test_intent: Change one approved DCMI DHCP/discovery configuration parameter over the out-of-band interface, prove the intended state and connectivity effect, and recover the original state safely.
original_method: Keep the source LANPlus raw 0x2c 0x12 0xdc request and selector definitions, but execute only one specification-encoded value after a getter baseline, explicit approval and preparation for loss or movement of the current endpoint.
manual_activity: The network/BMC owner approves one exact selector/value and its expected address/discovery effect, provides immutable BMC identity, a maintenance window, an independent console or secondary path, bounded rediscovery rules and exact restoration.
required_inputs: Verified SUT/BMC firmware and immutable BMC identity
Current BMC address, VLAN, MAC and route
Approved DCMI specification/profile and matching encoder/decoder
Exactly one selector and revision/data payload
safety_requirements: No guessed selector or default value
Rediscover only within an allowlisted network and verify immutable identity
agent_execution_scope: Bind current endpoint to immutable target identity
Read and decode the selected baseline
Validate write and restore bytes against the approved profile
Re-establish the same BMC identity within bounds
Archive redacted session and recovery evidence
engineer_actions: Approve the selector/value and expected endpoint transition
Ensure independent access and network isolation
Own intervention after unexpected loss and final PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: A generic `dcmi set_conf_param` call does not prove the source raw bytes, and credential-bearing argv plus an unbounded follow-up against the old address cannot safely handle DHCP/discovery transition.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Capture the selector with the approved 0x13 getter; after approval, send one secret-safe LANPlus raw 0x2c 0x12 0xdc <selector> 0 <validated-data>, then rediscover only the same immutable BMC identity, read back and restore under the plan.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The five selector meanings, revision byte, OOB route and 10/5 timing remain preserved; exact values and reconnect assumptions are not invented.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Model the write as an endpoint-transition transaction: snapshot address and selector state, arm independent recovery, submit once, observe session loss, rediscover by allowlisted immutable identity, verify the value and restore deterministically.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds identity-safe disconnect/reconnect handling, secret controls and a verified rollback instead of accepting only command completion.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: The IB setter validates parameter semantics but cannot prove the behavior of the LANPlus session or remote reachability when its own network configuration changes.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Activating DHCP or changing discovery can strand management, land the BMC at an unexpected address, collide with another endpoint or cause automation to reconnect to the wrong device.

project_override_considerations: A vendor management tool is equivalent only if it exposes the exact changed selector, before/after bytes, endpoint transition and same-device identity proof; otherwise raw OOB coverage remains missing.
expected_evidence: Current address/VLAN/MAC plus raw getter baseline
Exact redacted write request/response and completion
Timestamped session loss or continuity and bounded rediscovery
Cryptographic or hardware-backed proof that the new endpoint is the same BMC
Post-change raw read-back and network-behavior result
No unrelated command or log-clear audit

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The Master consistently describes an OOB DCMI configuration write, provides its selector family and delegates variable bytes to a cited specification table. The placeholders and weak criterion are incomplete, and self-disconnection is an unhandled risk, but there is no internal semantic contradiction.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The setter and route are identifiable. Exact bytes, approval, baseline, independent access and recovery are concrete prerequisites, so the case remains REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION.

review_improvement: Turns a potentially self-disconnecting remote write into a single approved endpoint-transition transaction with identity-bound rediscovery, semantic verification and rollback.
independent_technical_reasoning: Unlike the in-band variant, this command can invalidate the very address and session carrying it. Success may therefore appear as a timeout, and a responding replacement address may belong to another device. Safe automation must treat disconnect as an expected but bounded transition, anchor reconnection to immutable identity, then verify the selector and restore without repeating the write.
